items.title: Section: How the Six Gateways Unlock One Another in Sequence

items.zh: 如是真義理門，由遠離二邊理門應隨決了。如其所應，證得、教導二種理門，由後二種不可思議、意趣理門應隨決了。問：如前說別義相應意趣者，此有何義？答：非如言音名身、句身、文身義相應意趣，但是除遣如言音等其餘勝義，是名別義相應意趣。復次，此中於真義理門，由遠離二邊理門隨決了已，便能證得所應得義。由能證得所得義故，所餘證得理門，由不可思議理門亦隨決了；又復一切諸佛世尊教導理門，由意趣理門亦隨決了；如是一切隨其所應。又若於彼真義理門隨決了者，當知能入五種離生。一、能入未離欲離生，二、能入倍離欲離生，三、能入已離欲離生，四、能入獨覺離生，五、能入菩薩離生。
items.en: Just as true meaning is discerned through the gateway of avoiding the two extremes, so, correspondingly, are the gateways of realisation and teaching discerned through the gateways of the inconceivable and of intention. Furthermore, discerning the gateway of true meaning allows entry into five kinds of certainty of realisation: entering while not yet free of desire, entering while doubly free of desire, entering while already free of desire, entering as a pratyekabuddha, and entering as a bodhisattva.

items.title: Section: Why Ultimate Truth Must Be Taught Alongside Conventional Truth

items.zh: 問：若安立諦建立為諦，何因緣故，更復顯示非安立諦？答：若離非安立諦，二種解脫不應道理。謂於相縛及麁重縛。
items.en: Question: if established truth is already established as truth, for what reason is non-established truth additionally revealed? Answer: without non-established truth, two kinds of liberation would not accord with reason, namely liberation from the bondage of characteristics and from the bondage of coarse afflictive residue.

items.title: Section: Why Concentration Alone, However Excellent, Cannot Free the Mind

items.zh: 若有行於諸安立諦，彼一切行皆行有相；行有相故。於諸相縛不得解脫；於諸相縛不解脫故，於麁重縛亦不解脫。若有行於非安立諦，不行於相；不行相故，於諸相縛便得解脫；於諸相縛得解脫故，於麁重縛亦得解脫。問：若唯由彼非安立諦，於一切縛解脫清淨，何緣顯示安立諦耶？答：為令資糧及方便道得清淨故。問：若即由彼行有相心，於二種縛解脫清淨，有何過失？答：若有極善定心，依第四靜慮順決擇分善法中轉，緣諸諦境；彼諸行者，於二種縛應得解脫究竟清淨，然不清淨，故不應理。又世間道、出世間道二種差別應不可立，然彼二道有相、無相有差別故，不應道理。
items.en: Whoever operates within established truths operates entirely among characteristics, and so cannot be liberated from the bondage of characteristics, nor, consequently, from the bondage of coarse residue. Whoever operates within non-established truth does not operate among characteristics, and so achieves liberation from the bondage of characteristics, and consequently from the bondage of coarse residue as well. Established truth is taught in order to purify the requisite path and the preparatory path. If one possessed excellent concentration within the fourth absorption, operating among the wholesome dharmas conducive to penetration, contemplating the truths, such a practitioner ought to achieve complete purity from both bonds, yet remains impure, which does not accord with reason. Moreover, no difference between the mundane and transcendent paths could then be established, though such a difference genuinely exists, which likewise does not accord with reason.

items.title: Section: Five Faces of Coarse Residue, and a New Territory Opens

items.zh: 謂若略說，無所堪能不調柔相，是麁重相。此無堪能不調柔相，復有五相。一、現重相，二、剛強相，三、障礙相，四、怯劣相，五、不自在轉無堪能相。由有此相，順雜染品、違清淨品相續而住，是故說為無所堪能不調柔相。復次，有五諸根大種長養。謂食長養、夢長養、避不平等長養、梵行長養、等至長養。即此長養略有二種。一、任持長養，二、不損害長養。此中最初是任持長養，後四是不損害長養。
items.en: Briefly stated, an incapacity and inflexibility is the mark of coarse residue. This incapacity and inflexibility further unfolds into five marks: the mark of heaviness, of rigidity, of obstruction, of timidity, and of lacking mastery and capability. The above concludes the decisive discernment embracing the noble teaching's own meaning. Furthermore, there are five nourishments of the faculties and elements: nourishment through food, through sleep, through avoiding imbalance, through pure conduct, and through meditative attainment. These nourishments are, briefly, of two kinds: sustaining nourishment, and nourishment that prevents harm.

items.title: Section: Four Ways Food Itself Sustains a Living Being

items.zh: 任持長養略有四種。一、變壞任持，二、喜悅任持，三、希望任持，四、攝受執取任持。復次，有五種行。一、身行，二、語行，三、意行，四、業行，五、壽行。
items.en: Sustaining nourishment is, briefly, of four kinds: nourishment through transformation, through joy, through hope, and through grasping and holding. Furthermore, there are five activities: bodily activity, verbal activity, mental activity, karmic activity, and life activity.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Heedfulness for the Householder, Ten for the Renunciant

items.zh: 復次，有五種不放逸。一、依在家品不放逸，二、依出家品不放逸，三、能遠離不善不放逸，四、能攝受諸善不放逸，五、修習相續不放逸。依在家品不放逸者，復有五種，如前已說。依出家品不放逸者，復有十種，如聲聞地決擇毘奈耶相應中，我當廣說。
items.en: Furthermore, there are five kinds of heedfulness: heedfulness according with the householder's own life, heedfulness according with the renunciant's own life, heedfulness able to avoid the unwholesome, heedfulness able to embrace the wholesome, and heedfulness of sustained cultivation. Heedfulness according with the householder's life is, further, of five kinds, already explained elsewhere. Heedfulness according with the renunciant's life is, further, of ten kinds, to be extensively explained in the decisive discernment corresponding to monastic discipline in the Grounds of Śrāvakas.

items.zh: 能遠離不善不放逸者，當知即是前二正斷。能攝受諸善不放逸者，當知即是後二正斷。修習相續不放逸者，謂於善法無間、殷重精勤修習。復次，名有五種。一、心，二、心所有法，三、善，四、不善，五、無記。

blocks.text: The six gateways of the inner science are tied together, and the treatise explains why the truth beyond words must be taught at all.
Master Cháng Bǎi: having earlier, as an ordinary being, subdued six grades of desire-realm affliction is being "doubly free" of desire.

Without non-established truth, liberation from the two bonds (of marks and of coarse heaviness) would not be possible. Master Cháng Bǎi: while the mind still holds the form of words, one is not freed of the two bonds.
Heaviness, rigidity, obstruction, timidity, and lacking mastery. Master Cháng Bǎi: with afflictive seeds, one considers oneself unable to practise and does not lift oneself up.
Sustaining through transformation, joy, hope, and holding: matched to the four foods.
(Untranslated, 0657b09: heedfulness that avoids the unwholesome is the first two right efforts; that which embraces the good, the last two; continuous heedfulness is unbroken, earnest practice.)
"While the mind still holds the form of words, it is not free." Teaching uses words; freedom does not.

quiz.q: How many entries does discerning the gateway of true meaning allow?
options: three: śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattva, one for each vehicle
two: worldly and transcendent
ten: one for each ground
five: not yet free of desire, doubly free, already free, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattva
quiz.why: The treatise lists entering while not yet free of desire, doubly free, and already free, then entering as a pratyekabuddha and as a bodhisattva. Three śrāvaka entries are distinguished by degree of freedom from desire.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the entry while doubly free of desire?
options: having subdued six grades of desire-realm defilement, one skips stream entry and directly reaches the second fruit
freed twice, first from the desire realm and then from the form realm, so that on entering the path one is an arhat at once
first taking lay precepts, then renunciant ones
spending double the time before seeing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having earlier, as an ordinary being, subdued six grades of desire-realm defilement is called doubly free; on now entering the path, one bypasses stream entry and directly realises the second fruit.

quiz.q: Why is non-established truth revealed in addition to established truth?
options: so that other paths cannot object, for established truth already suffices for all liberation and the other is only a defence against doubts about names
to explain differences among the three realms
without it, liberation from the bonds of characteristics and of coarse residue would not accord with reason
to increase the number of truths
quiz.why: The treatise answers that without non-established truth two liberations would not accord with reason, namely from the bondage of characteristics and from that of coarse residue. The answer concerns liberation, not debate.

quiz.q: What are the five marks of incapacity and inflexibility?
options: body, speech, mind, affliction, and karma, these being where coarse residue dwells
greed, hatred, delusion, pride, and doubt
heaviness, rigidity, obstruction, timidity, and lacking mastery and capability
dullness, restlessness, laziness, forgetfulness, and distraction
quiz.why: The treatise lists the marks of heaviness, rigidity, obstruction, timidity, and lacking mastery and capability. Together they spell out coarse residue, briefly defined as incapacity and inflexibility of body and mind.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the mark of timidity?
options: the body feels heavy and wants only to sleep after sitting down, caused by overeating
not daring to debate other paths
fearing death and so avoiding renunciation
with afflictive seeds, one thinks oneself unable to practise the path and does not lift oneself up
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having afflictive seeds, one considers oneself unable to practise the noble path and does not lift oneself up; this is the mark of timidity, one of the five of coarse residue.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain nourishment through avoiding imbalance?
options: refusing a society of unequal wealth and working for equal treatment of beings
avoiding imbalance of body and mind, so the elements stay in order and emotion in check
avoiding people of unequal rank
cultivating equanimity towards friend and foe alike
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: avoiding a state of imbalance in body and mind, not letting the four elements fall out of harmony or emotion run out of control, can nourish the faculties and elements.

quiz.q: This is rendered "excellent concentration within the fourth absorption, contemplating the truths." What key point is dropped?
options: nothing: 順決擇分 is merely another name for the fourth absorption
順決擇分善法: even at the preparatory stage, still with marks, one remains ordinary
諸諦 is dropped
第四 is dropped
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having marks means the mind still holds the form of words, so one is not freed of the two bonds; though at the preparatory stage, one is still ordinary. The omitted phrase carries the argument.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of sustaining nourishment?
options: through food, sleep, pure conduct, and attainment
through earth, water, fire, and wind
through transformation, joy, hope, and grasping and holding
through body, speech, mind, and life
quiz.why: The treatise lists sustaining through transformation, joy, hope, and grasping and holding. The lecture matches them to the four foods, with solid food changing in the belly and sustaining the faculties.
